--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent behavior probes: against one_D_TFT ... Parent against one_D_TFT: after initial 10 CC, opponent one initial D then TFT? It recovers well. four_D_TFT: parent gets 0.875, never recovers (mutual coop 0). So parent fails against four_D_TFT."
STRATEGY: The parent is a mostly-cooperative, randomly-forgiving strategy that retaliates after opponent defections. The trace simulates the parent against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and against the listed population strategies. It proposes changing the parent to a more forgiving strategy that tolerates up to four consecutive opponent defections, switches to defection only after five consecutive defections, and adds occasional probing/exploitation of always-cooperative opponents.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 2.75. So slightly better." / "Parent got 0.875. So slightly worse." / "Parent got 2.1125 against periodic_D. So we are worse."
STRATEGY: The parent strategy cooperates initially, forgives short opponent defection streaks, punishes long streaks, and probes/defects periodically based on recent opponent defection rates and retaliation history. The trace simulates this parent against probe opponents including one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, sustained_D, and periodic_D, then revises it by adding adaptive retaliation tracking, changing probe frequency, and altering defection responses to improve cumulative tournament fitness.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 2.1125. So we are worse against periodic_D."
STRATEGY: Parent is a mostly-cooperative adaptive strategy that forgives short defection streaks, punishes long ones, and probes based on retaliation rate. The trace simulates it against TFT, four_D_TFT, sustained_D, and periodic_D, then revises it to defect on the first D of a streak when past retaliation is low and to use adaptive exploitation rates.
